profile.name: Apu Inka
profile.tagline: A Peruvian folk dance re-enacting the capture of the Inca by Spanish invaders.
profile.insight: In the Sapallanga District of Huancayo, dancers annually re-enact the capture of the Inca by Spanish invaders during the September feast of the Virgen de Cocharcas.
profile.profile: Apu Inka is a Peruvian folk dance that dramatizes the historical capture of the Inca by Spanish forces. Primarily performed during the annual September festival of the Virgen de Navidad or Virgen de Cocharcas in the Sapallanga District of the Junín Region, the dance serves as a cultural performance of historical memory. It is classified as an indigenous American dance and is also performed in various other regions across Peru.
profile.profile_long: Apu Inka is a folk dance originating from Peru, categorized as an indigenous American dance. The name itself is derived from the Quechua language, where 'apu' refers to an Andean deity and 'Inka' refers to the Inca. The primary function of the dance is to re-enact the historical capture of the Inca by Spanish invaders, serving as a performative narrative of this significant colonial encounter. The dance is most prominently associated with the annual feast held in honor of the Virgen de Navidad or the Virgen de Cocharcas. This event takes place every September in the Sapallanga District, located within the Huancayo Province of the Junín Region. While this district is the primary site of the performance, the dance is not limited to this location and is performed in other regions of Peru as well. Due to the limited nature of the current documentation, specific details regarding the choreography, musical accompaniment, costume requirements, and the specific roles of the dancers remain undocumented in the sources. The dance is considered a living tradition, as it is held annually.
